claim_text: Wave impact, fast-moving water and scour are a separate mechanism from still-water inundation: they act by force and undermining, depend on wave height or flow speed rather than depth, and depend strongly on site exposure, foundation and soil. They are excluded from flood_inundation_contact and deferred, with wave damage withheld rather than set to zero.
exact_locator: flood_wind D-FW-07 and FW-C012 (scour, erosion, debris and wave loading excluded; foundation withheld not zero); flood_solar FS_FOUND (T4 velocity/scour placeholder); Hazus 7.0 section 5.4.1.1.2.1 (BCAR coastal curves assume waves of 1.5 ft or more destroy walls); NACCS 2015 publishes wave and erosion tables separately from inundation
permitted_inference: Keep the still-water curves wave-free; record wave-inclusive curves (FEMA DF 658, NACCS wave tables) as candidates for the deferred pathway.
prohibited_inference: Use a wave-inclusive curve in the still-water pathway; treat absent wave damage as zero; add an unreviewed placeholder curve.
reasoning: Avoids double counting when a wave pathway is added and avoids overstating sheltered coastal flooding. Hazard's coastal grid supplies surge depth only, so a wave curve would have no input today.
update_trigger: Hazard supplies wave height or flow speed, and wave or velocity curves are curated.
